name: Desert folk
one_line: Water is the whole craft: a reed in wet sand, a ditch from the stream, a tunnel under the hills; salt for the road, and a fire the size of a hat against the coldest night in the world.

needs: water within reach: a soak in wet sand, a spring, a stream, or a qanat line
shade (an overhang, a palm, poles for a ramada) and brush to burn; the camp is only as big as its firewood walk

staples: grass seed ground on the stone (ricegrass, grama)
maize, beans and squash on the watered plot
cactus fruit and pads; agave hearts from the pit
dates at the oasis; hare and lizard everywhere
how: a channel from the stream to the plot; a check dam of stones across the wash
seed knocked into a basket, ground on a slab
saguaro fruit hooked down with a rib pole
agave hearts roasted two days in a stone-lined pit
a reed in wet sand where there is no open water
preserve: sun-drying: fruit, meat strips, everything dries in a day
the pot and the mud storeroom: seed and flour sealed against mice

fuel.note: almost none: tiny hoarded fires of brush, dead cactus rib and dung; a canyon adds branch from the stream gallery and the oasis palm frond. No lamp, no torch technique: the desert teaches water, not light, and the desert night is the coldest dark in the game

shelter.form: a flat-roofed block of mud-and-stone rooms that grows a room at a time, ladders to the roof, a ramada of poles and brush for the shade, a storeroom; in a canyon the rooms stack under the overhang

HOT_DESERT.fuel: dead cactus rib, brush, mesquite twig
HOT_DESERT.food: mesquite pods, saguaro fruit, prickly pear, hare
HOT_DESERT.shelter: a ramada of poles and brush; mud walls only where a wash gives clay
HOT_DESERT.palette: buff, creosote green, saguaro green, rust rock

COLD_DESERT.food: ricegrass seed on the grinding stone, saltbush seed, hare; a thin year
COLD_DESERT.shelter: a pit house dug into the ground against the freezing night, brush roof over it
COLD_DESERT.palette: grey-green, alkali white, blue shadow, frost

OASIS.food: dates and figs, the channel-fed plot of grain and beans
OASIS.shelter: mud-brick houses in the palm shade, roofed with palm trunk and frond; channels between the plots
OASIS.palette: palm green, mud gold, water blue, white sand

CANYON.fuel: branch from the cottonwood gallery, juniper, pinyon
CANYON.food: maize, beans and squash on check-dammed plots, pinyon nuts, the seasonal stream's fish
CANYON.shelter: cliff dwellings of stacked sandstone under the overhang, a kiva sunk in the ledge
CANYON.palette: red sandstone, cottonwood gold, juniper green, deep shadow

BADLANDS.fuel: sagebrush, juniper from the ravines, dung
BADLANDS.food: grama and ricegrass seed on the stone, prickly pear, yucca fruit; hunting on the flats
BADLANDS.shelter: dug into the clay bank and daubed with it; sumac and juniper poles
BADLANDS.palette: banded clay: grey, ochre, rust; fossil-bone white

SALT_FLAT.food: salt and nothing else: glasswort and saltgrass seed at the margin; food walks in from elsewhere
SALT_FLAT.shelter: a brush windbreak on the rim; nobody sleeps on the crust

knows: mesquite: pods to flour, roots to the water table
saguaro, prickly pear and agave: which month the fruit comes, how to skin a pad, why the agave heart is pit-roasted
Indian ricegrass and grama: seed for the stone
date palm and fig at the oasis; pinyon in the canyon
plantkeeper.teaches_flavour: why the dead canal still greens; why mesquite is the desert's tree; the year the saguaro fruits and the year it does not
plantkeeper.teaches_practical: shade and water before food: the sun kills in a day, hunger in a month; which cactus is a cup; agave raw will hurt you; creosote smells of rain because rain is coming

works: ochre and mineral paint; beeweed boiled black
makes: painted jars: black on white, red on buff
water jars, seed jars, corrugated cooking pots
wants_from_player: brush and dung for the firing

techniques.name: Water from sand
techniques.verb: push a hollow reed through a grass filter into damp sand at a soak, tamp, wait, suck; fill ostrich eggshells, stopper them with grass, bury the cache for the way back
techniques.teaches: the headman gives this first because it is the one thing every desert camp knows, oasis or salt flat: the channel needs a stream, the sip-well needs only wet sand. It turns the desert from a wall into a road
techniques.unlocks: drink at a soak with no open water; eggshell canteens: water carried and cached

techniques.name: Channel
techniques.verb: cut a ditch from the stream to the plot, a hand's drop in a hundred paces; a check dam of stones across a wash holds the storm's silt and water
techniques.teaches: water is the crop: bring it and the seed does the rest. Some dug three hundred miles of ditch with sticks and baskets and the modern town still runs on their lines
techniques.unlocks: a plot away from the bank counts as watered (a rule, not fluid physics); the crop ceiling at an oasis or a canyon stream

techniques.name: Qanat
techniques.verb: a mother well at the foot of the hills, a tunnel sloped a hair downhill for miles, dug from a line of shafts; the water walks out into daylight at the village having never seen the sun
techniques.teaches: centuries of water without a pump and without a drop lost to the sun; the line of spoil rings on the surface is how you find one, and how the ruin is read
techniques.unlocks: a desert camp's water and its plots where no stream reaches; a restored qanat is the largest inheritance in the desert

techniques.name: Salt pans
techniques.verb: scrape the crust of the flat, or pool brine in a shallow pan and let the sun take the water
techniques.teaches: salt keeps food and is the desert's coin: it walks out on the road and pots, grain and dried fish walk back

techniques.name: Knapping
techniques.verb: strike flakes off obsidian or flint with a hammerstone; press the edge sharp with an antler tine
techniques.teaches: the sharpest edge in the world, made in a minute and thrown away; the knapping floor glitters for ten thousand years
techniques.unlocks: a knife: dress carcasses, cut cordage, split cactus fruit

techniques.name: Cordage and baskets
techniques.verb: beat and twist yucca or agave leaf into cord; coil a basket so tight, pitched, that it holds water
techniques.teaches: the desert's rope and its baskets: a burden basket on a tumpline carries the harvest home; sandals of the same fibre
techniques.unlocks: carry more (burden); snares, sandals, a net for the hare drive

techniques.name: Ochre
techniques.verb: grind red and yellow earth on a stone with a little fat
techniques.teaches: paint for the pot, the rock and the skin; a handprint on the overhang is the oldest signature there is
techniques.unlocks: mark your own trail beside the forgotten waymarks; sunscreen

techniques.name: Mud and stone
techniques.verb: puddle clay with straw and water, lay it in courses or bricks on a stone footing, plaster it; roof with poles and brush and a hand of mud
techniques.teaches: a house that is cool at noon and warm at midnight, and a storeroom that mice and sun cannot open; the walls outlast the roof by centuries
techniques.unlocks: the camp's storage rung and its rooms; wall stubs and a melted mound are the ruin

wants: dried fish and grain off the road

ladder: a fire of brush in the lee of a rock, hoarded
water: the soak and the eggshell cache; then the channel from the stream, and the plot (crop)
the storeroom: mud walls, pots, dried fruit and seed
salt goes out on the road; pots, grain and fish come back
growth.restraint: the channel takes what the stream gives in a wet year and is cut back in a dry one; the mesquite is never felled, only its pods taken; a soak is covered against animals and never drunk dry; a camp that outruns its brush burns its roof poles next, and then the dark
growth.ceiling_hint: with water to bring — an oasis, a canyon stream, a qanat — the desert reaches the tribal ceiling and a town of mud rooms; away from water the camp stays a foraging handful that moves between soaks and never plants. Herding (the Bedouin's desert) is the herd fundamental, built last, not this life

signatures.what: a shallow straight trough across the flat, greener than the ground beside it, from where a stream was to where a field was
signatures.restore: cleared: the camp re-cuts the ditch on the old line
signatures.inherits: a watered plot from the first season; the grade is already right

signatures.what: a line of low doughnut mounds marching straight from the hills, each a filled shaft; a dry tunnel under them
signatures.restore: restored: a shaft re-dug and the tunnel cleared of silt, the water runs again
signatures.inherits: water where there is no stream: the largest head start in the desert

signatures.what: stacked sandstone rooms under an overhang, roofs gone, soot on the rock above, a round pit that was a kiva
signatures.restore: restored: the camp roofs the rooms with poles and brush
signatures.inherits: walls and shade; the coldest night's best shelter

signatures.what: knee-high wall stubs of stone and mud in a grid on a rise, a mound of melted adobe, sherds everywhere
signatures.restore: restored: new courses on old footings
signatures.inherits: level floors and a storeroom's footprint; the sherd scatter points at the clay, so the potter comes sooner

signatures.what: by a soak: a hearth stain, white eggshell fragments (some engraved), and a grinding slab with a hollow polished by seed, its muller beside it, left for whoever came next
signatures.restore: restored: the camp's own eggshell cache goes into the same sand; the slab is roughened and used again
signatures.inherits: the soak itself, proof that water can be had here; seed flour from the first harvest

signatures.what: ochre handprints and figures on the overhang wall; pecked spirals on the varnished boulder
signatures.restore: restored: the camp paints beside them, never over them
signatures.inherits: waymarks: the paintings point at the water

ruin.plants_differ: the old canal line greens with mesquite, saltbush and grass long after it runs dry; where fields were over-watered a salt crust grows only glasswort; date palms outlive the people who planted them by a century

aesthetic.silhouette: a flat-roofed block of rooms with ladders, a ramada's flat shade, the straight line of a channel; under a canyon wall, rooms stacked like a wasp's nest
sounds: a small fire in a big silence
props: a channel with a wooden head gate
a ramada and ladders to the roof
painted pots and a sherd scatter
an eggshell cache and salt cakes

real_world.region: Salt and Gila river valleys, Phoenix basin, Arizona, c. 450–1450 CE
real_world.note: some 300 miles of hand-dug main canals in the Phoenix basin alone, watering a quarter-million acres at grades of a few feet a mile; maize, beans, squash, cotton and agave; red-on-buff pottery; floods in the 1300s wrecked the canal heads and the system was left by c. 1450. The Akimel and Tohono O'odham are their likely descendants, and Phoenix's modern canals follow their lines

real_world.region: Colorado Plateau, cliff dwellings c. 1190–1280 CE
real_world.note: some 600 cliff dwellings of sandstone and adobe mortar under the overhangs, with kivas; dry farming of maize, beans and squash on the mesa top, with over a thousand check dams and hundreds of terraces holding each storm's soil and water, and reservoirs; left in the drought of 1276–99. Their descendants are the Hopi, Zuni and Rio Grande pueblos, who still coil, paint and open-fire their pottery

real_world.region: Iran, from about 3,000 years ago; spread as karez, foggara, khettara and falaj
real_world.note: a mother well at the foot of the hills and a tunnel sloped downhill for kilometres (most under 5 km, one near Kerman about 70 km), dug from vertical shafts every 20–35 m whose spoil rings mark the line across the surface like a string of craters; no pump, no evaporation; kept by muqannis whose trade passed father to son; eleven listed by UNESCO in 2016

sip-wells: a hollow stem with a grass filter pushed into wet sand and sucked; water carried in stoppered ostrich eggshells and buried in caches along the way; tsamma melons and water tubers. Engraved eggshell canteens at Diepkloof Rock Shelter are about 60,000 years old

soaks (native wells) dug metres down through sand to seepage and covered with branches against animals, every one named and its place taught; grass and acacia seed ground to flour on a slab with a muller and baked as damper; big grindstones left at camps for the next visit — Australian grindstone fragments are about 30,000 years old

real_world.analogue: Nabataean and Byzantine Negev farms (Avdat, Shivta)
real_world.region: Negev highlands, c. 3rd century BCE – 7th century CE
real_world.note: runoff farming on about 100 mm of rain a year: hillside catchments, channels and stone terraces across the wadi that hold each winter flood's water and silt, cisterns, and grape mounds; Evenari's reconstructed farms at Avdat and Shivta from the late 1950s proved the yields
